scope: Compositional finite WM semantics: typed evidence roles, scoped NARS revision, ProbLog/MLN factor readouts, and calibrated BN deduction certificates
limitations: Deterministic program interpretation uses least-model semantics and is not an executable general program compiler; the concrete finite-table compiler is executable once supplied a table.
Canonical Boolean table clauses can be exponential and use zero potentials; finite real log-weights alone do not express hard zeros.
Mixture table revision is distinct from factor multiplication and program union.
NARS interpretation uses core revision; the capped runtime formula has distinct count semantics.
Source-world accuracy is separate from within-model conditional dependence.
The balanced CMI certificate uses natural logarithms and positive source-query mass.
Native CPT multisets average conditional answers rather than conditioning a joint mixture; their certificate retains the nonlinear aggregation gap.
Averaged conditional readouts need not admit a joint realization; the new incompatibility counterexample uses finite joint tables, not an instantiated CPT witness.
Factor-entry indices are local to their supplied table; native abstract graph indexing is chosen noncomputably.
Operation counts describe the reference tree evaluator and do not qualify a CeTTa implementation or native runtime cost.
qualification_kind: Scoped build, strict module checks, actual module-data equality, evaluator controls, kernel axiom audit, and before/after source and owned-file snapshots
verification_scope: Listed modules and owned files; the local dependency sources have a separate hash inventory.
